subject.title: Agent loop allows simulated tool calls instead of enforcing real tool invocation

question: Should OpenClaw default to strict structured tool-call protocol enforcement, or keep bounded plain-text tool-call promotion for local-model compatibility?
rationale: The code path is small enough to change, but the choice affects a security boundary and could intentionally break existing local-model deployments that depend on promotion.

options.title: Default strict protocol
options.body: Disable or default-off text-to-tool-call promotion, keep warning/scrubbing for fake calls, and require users to fix provider parsing or opt into a clearly named compatibility mode.

options.title: Keep bounded promotion
options.body: Preserve exact-name standalone text promotion but require stronger provenance, before_tool_call/ledger proof, and docs that make the security tradeoff explicit.

options.title: Defer to hard-gate design
options.body: Leave this issue open as a narrow input into the broader pre-response enforcement design tracked in the related hard-gate issue.

recommendation.title: Default strict protocol
recommendation.body: Disable or default-off text-to-tool-call promotion, keep warning/scrubbing for fake calls, and require users to fix provider parsing or opt into a clearly named compatibility mode.
